adds.title: Italy 'to open first prison for transgender inmates' | BBC News
adds.summary: BBC News (12 Jan 2010): Italy announced plans for one of the world's first dedicated transgender prisons at Pozzale, near Florence - converting a nearly empty medium-security women's prison into a specially equipped detention centre for about 30 of Italy's roughly 60 transgender prisoners (mostly convicted of drug or prostitution offences); gay-rights groups welcomed the dedicated space and its psychological support. The report states that until then transgender prisoners had been located in women's prisons 'where they are often segregated for their own safety' - the documented 2010 baseline for placement practice in Italy. Repubblica (2013) later reported the Pozzale project was abandoned.

adds.title: La doppia sofferenza delle trans in carcere | La Repubblica (Inchieste)
adds.summary: La Repubblica investigative report 'La doppia sofferenza delle trans in carcere' (28 Aug 2013): at that date the prison administration counted 69 transsexual prisoners spread across ten Italian facilities, with placement tracking legal sex - female hormones could not be prescribed to prisoners who 'according to their identity card, count as men,' trans women were held in men's sections, and those who had already undergone sex-change surgery were 'destined for the women's sections.' Segregation practice: in some prisons trans prisoners were put in isolation when cells were lacking - described as the most inhumane way to preserve their safety - and protected sections such as the G8 section at Rebibbia (Rome) and the protected section at Poggioreale (Naples) imposed limitations, including on partner visits. Documented ruling: the 2011 Terni case in which the Spoleto surveillance magistrate ordered the local health authority to pay for the prisoner's hormone therapy 'to guarantee psychophysical integrity'; the ruling was appealed and followed by a July 2012 appellate decision. The dedicated Pozzale transgender prison project (2008-2010), which would have drawn trans women from the special wing of Sollicciano (Florence), was shelved.

records.note: National practice (applies to this region; no Nord-Ovest-specific placement documentation found in this search round): Italian placement follows legal sex as recorded on identity documents - trans women without completed legal sex change are held in men's sections and may be denied female-hormone prescriptions because they 'count as men' on paper, while those who completed surgery/legal change are assigned to women's sections (Repubblica, 2013). Protective segregation takes the form of protected sections (Rebibbia G8, Poggioreale) or, when cells are lacking, isolation described as the most inhumane safety measure. One documented ruling: Terni case, Spoleto surveillance magistrate ordering the ASL to fund hormone care (2011, appellate ruling July 2012). A dedicated trans unit at Pozzale was announced in 2010 (BBC) but never opened.
